classification.difficultyReason: Apply the taught sine-rule procedure, check the supplementary angle and sketch both possible triangles.

content.prompt:
A triangle $ABC$ has $AB=3\text{ cm}$, $AC=2\text{ cm}$ and $\angle B=35^\circ$.

Find the two possible values of $\angle C$ correct to 1 decimal place and sketch the triangles.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\frac{\sin C}{3}&=\frac{\sin35^\circ}{2}\\\sin C&=\frac{3\sin35^\circ}{2}\\C_1&=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{3\sin35^\circ}{2}\right)\\C_1&\approx59.35755096^\circ\\C_2&=180^\circ-C_1\\C_2&\approx120.64244904^\circ\end{align*}$$
Both are possible because $35^\circ+59.35755096^\circ<180^\circ$ and $35^\circ+120.64244904^\circ<180^\circ$.

Therefore $\angle C=59.4^\circ$ or $120.6^\circ$, correct to 1 decimal place. The two sketches are shown below.

spec.description: Paired answer-only sketches, with A lower left, B above and C lower right in the acute case; A lower left, B upper right and C below-left of B in the obtuse case. Ordinary marks use house black.
spec.mathematics: Both triangles have AB=3 cm, AC=2 cm and angle B=35 degrees. Angle C is respectively 59.4 degrees and 120.6 degrees. Coordinates derive from the two sine-rule solutions.
